role_and_message.evidence: The M example retains the motivation for grounding specific long-tail objects in a complex scene, plus phone and fork examples.

panel_and_object_coverage.evidence: All three full photographs and all original white detection boxes remain; the only extra view is an exact enlargement of the bottle strip from the same top image.

labels_math_and_numbers.evidence: Mountain Dew, Phone and Fork identities match source labels. No new numerical metric or invented baseline result image is included.

connections_and_direction.evidence: The detail crop is explicitly identified as the same detections, retaining correspondence to the top photograph; the lower examples remain separate categories.

visual_encodings.evidence: White boxes still indicate original target detections. Existing box coordinates, including partial boundary boxes, are preserved without adding annotations to the image.

examples_and_data.evidence: Three original full-image regions match native pixels, and the added bottle detail matches exact2×nearest source pixels independently.

unsupported_additions.evidence: The SearchDet-every-instance/GroundingDINO-missing-bottles comparison is explicitly limited to this scene as in the Figure1 caption. The headline and white-box legend describe existing content.

complete_visible_content.evidence: All photos, detection boxes and category labels are visible. The enlargement preserves source blur rather than inventing sharper bottle details.

remaining_limitations: Original illustrative examples, labels and resolution remain; added explanatory text is bounded to source claims. This is not a new verification of scientific correctness.
caption:
Figure 1. Detection results for label “Mountain Dew”. While the
GroundingDINO, one of the state-of-the-art grounded object de-
tection methods, fails to capture the Mountain Dew bottles in the
image displayed in the figure, SearchDet manages to ground every
instance of Mountain Dew that appears in the image. Detection
results for other classes “Phone” and “Fork”.
